title: Even parts, knotless braids and safe tension
course_title: Hair Care & Simple Styling: Salon Service Practice

say: Even parts, knotless braids and safe tension.
This is the video for module 3 of Hair Care and Simple Styling.
Clients judge a style first by its parts. Even parts also mean even weight, so no small section is strained.
In a square grid, the parts line up like a chessboard. Very neat when tied up, but lines of scalp show when the braids hang loose.

panel.heading: Square grid or brick-lay
left: Parts line up front to back
right: Each row shifted half a section

say: In brick-lay, each row is shifted by half a section, like bricks in a wall, so the scalp is covered better when the braids hang down. Choose the pattern with the client.

panel.heading: Square grid or brick-lay
left: Parts line up front to back
right: Each row shifted half a section

say: Start at the nape. Draw the first row and clip all the hair above it away.

say: For example, Aisha in Kano plans medium box braids in brick-lay, with 8 rows. Four rows hold 10 braids, which is 40. The four shifted rows hold 9 each, which is 36.

panel.heading: Count before you quote
items: 4 rows of 10 braids = 40 braids
4 shifted rows of 9 braids = 36 braids
Total: 76 braids
76 x 6 minutes = 456 minutes

say: That is 76 braids. At her timed 6 minutes each, that is 456 minutes, about 7 hours 36 minutes of braiding. Now she can quote the time and buy the right hair.

say: Knotless braids look natural at the root because the weight builds slowly. Start with 2 or 3 stitches of her own hair only, firm but painless.

panel.heading: Building one knotless braid
items: Braid 2 or 3 stitches with her own hair only
Lay a thin, folded feed-in piece over the braid
Braid a few stitches, add the next piece
Stop adding at the agreed thickness
Check: no poking hairs, no tug at the root

say: Lay a thin piece of extension hair, folded in half, over the braid so each half joins a side strand.

say: Braid 2 or 3 more stitches, then add the next piece the same way.

say: For example, Tola in Lagos plans 60 knotless braids with 3 pieces each. That is 180 pieces. She gets about 30 pieces from one pack, so she needs 6 packs, plus one spare.
One pack costs about 1,200 naira.
So 7 packs cost about 8,400 naira. She tells the client in advance and writes it on the record card.
Many stylists seal synthetic ends in hot water, and it burns quickly. Put a towel on her neck and shoulders, ask her to lean away, and keep the kettle away from children.

cards.d: Towel on her neck and shoulders. She leans away. Kettle on a stable surface, away from children.
Hold the cup well below her shoulders and dip only the ends. No open flame near her head.
Cool it under clean running water. Seek medical help for anything more than a small, mild burn.

say: Hold the cup yourself, well below her shoulders, and dip only the ends. Never pour hot water over braids near her skin. Synthetic hair can catch fire, so never use a lighter near her head.

say: If skin is burned, cool it under clean running water, and seek medical help for anything more than a small, mild burn.

say: Traction alopecia is hair loss from repeated pulling. It often starts at the temples, and long-term pulling can make it permanent.
If she winces or says it hurts, stop and redo that section more loosely.

panel.heading: Signs the style is too tight
items: She winces or says it hurts
Skin lifts in little tents at the braid base
Redness around many bases
Bumps or soreness days later
Thinning temples over months

say: If the skin lifts in little tents, redo the braid. The scalp should lie flat.

say: Redness around many bases? Loosen the tightest rows before she leaves.

say: Bumps days later mean the tight braids should come out. Refer her if there is pus.

say: Thinning temples over months mean no tension at the hairline at all.

panel.heading: Signs the style is too tight

say: Run this check at the start, on every row, and before she leaves. Ask about past pain. Leave the hairline free and start cornrows thin. No tenting, no pain.
The course notes dermatologists advise extensions for 2 or 3 months at most, so agree a takedown date and remind her a week before.

panel.heading: Tension check
items: Ask about past pain
Hairline left free
No scalp tenting
No pain on any row
Takedown date agreed

say: To remember. Even parts mean even weight. Count braids and hair packs before you quote. Add extension weight gradually. Seal ends safely. And if it hurts, it is too tight. A child should never leave your chair in pain.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Even parts mean even weight
Count braids and packs before you quote
Knotless and feed-ins add weight gradually
Hot water: towel, distance, ends only, no flame
If it hurts, it is too tight: redo it

say: Now practise. Part a head in both patterns and count the braids. Install ten knotless braids and time each one. Then do four feed-in cornrows, asking for a comfort score after each row.
